scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported Anasazi record spans 800 to 1000 CE and has an excessively broad southwestern/western polygon extending well beyond the Four Corners. This card establishes the intended Ancestral Pueblo identity, not the accuracy of that geometry. The map interval is coverage only; the geometry remains a known research problem.
Naming follows Laguna Pueblo ranger Thelma Jean Atsye’s publicly available transcript. No literal translation of Anasazi is needed, and the older term remains an alias. The tour audio was not played.

The period sequence follows selected local developments at Mesa Verde and Pueblo Bonito. These are not universal phase boundaries or founding/fall dates of one government. Gaps are deliberate where this card provides no selected phase.

The early brochure’s indexed text and illustrated pithouse caption were read. A reconstruction is presented as such. The brochure’s speculative causal explanations and assertion of declining basketry quality are not repeated.

The museum grinding-stone and olla pages describe functions but provide no excavation provenience or artifact-specific date. The card acknowledges that limitation. The gallery’s exact maize introduction date, numerical dietary/household estimates and global production rankings are not used.
Bandelier’s yucca account supplies manufacturing practices, not dated finds at Mesa Verde. Claims about hair regrowth, medicinal efficacy and modern nutrient comparisons are omitted.

The NPS cacao account was read. Five sherds were tested, with theobromine found in three interpreted as cylinder jars, dated by decorative styles to 1000 to 1125 CE. Cacao-drink use is attributed to the researchers, not presented as a complete recipe or proof that all residents shared the practice. Other Mesoamerican ceremonial details are not projected onto Chaco.

The Square Tower House transcript distinguishes surviving structures and reported finds. Nearby early souvenir discoveries are not all reassigned to a specific room or archaeological context. No restricted ceremonial knowledge is reproduced.

Pueblo migration is distinguished from disappearance. Multiple descendant communities are acknowledged without collapsing their identities or manufacturing a political successor. No successor link is added because a single target would be misleading.
Independent historical review and depth certification remain pending; no older review is treated as covering this new narrative.
